problems: Owned list was empty: 23 states chosen from the group scope, the counterparts ea-02-a/b/c/d asked ea-02-x for, and pages opened along the way; several are under the ten-year line (zhang-chu, gongsun-zan, huainan, liu-yong, zhang-bu, peng-chong, yuan-shu) because earlier parts flagged them.

WebFetch returned URL_NOT_FOUND for Wei_Xiao, Wei_Ao, Dou_Rong (also the mobile host) and Deng_Zhi_(general); Peng_Chong, Zhang_Er, Song_Jian resolve to modern people; Liu_Zhang and Lu_Fang are disambiguations. The Wei Ao, Peng Chong, Zhang Bu, Liu Yong and Dou Rong dossiers therefore rest on the Emperor Guangwu page plus one or two others and are thin.

None of the new states is cut out of ea-02-c's Han Dynasty shapes (han-dynasty_184..215) or out of Cliopatria's Cao Cao shape: the rendering agents must carve the warlord, rebel and 23-36 regimes from the Han for their years.

sun-ce (195-206) is continuous with Cliopatria's Eastern Wu row (207-282, ea-03); ea-03 should decide whether to extend eastern-wu back to 195 and drop sun-ce. Cliopatria's Eastern Wu shape for 207-237 does not reach Vietnam, so shi-xie is the only dossier giving Jiaozhi in 207-226 besides the Han row ea-02-c marked wrong (224-237).
changsha-kingdom merges the Eighteen Kingdoms' Hengshan (Wu Rui, flagged as 'hengshan' by ea-02-b) with the Han vassal Changsha, as one man ruled both (rename event at -202).
dou-rong ends 36 (Guangwu page) as in ea-02-c's han-dynasty, but the Hexi Corridor page dates his submission to 29: ea-02-c may add a vassal tie 29-36.
Several 'rename' events (zhang-bu 27, chengjia 25, liu-yong 25, yuan-shu 197, shi-xie 210) mark a title change or a change of overlord, not a new name; they move no land.
Coordinates for capitals and for the Yellow Turban base (Guangzong) are approximate modern town positions, flagged in each capital note.
